headline: 5,418 passengers stranded as 51 flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia are disrupted
summary: Flight restrictions at Saudi airports have led to widespread cancellations and delays, affecting thousands of travelers from Dhaka.
details: Saudi Arabian airport restrictions have caused the disruption of 51 flights from Dhaka to various destinations in the Kingdom, leaving 5,418 passengers stranded.
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the disruptions occurred between Saturday night and Monday afternoon.
Of the 51 affected flights, 12 were direct flights, including those operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Saudi Arabian Airlines, and Riyadh Air.
The remaining 39 flights were transit flights operated by carriers such as IndiGo, Emirates, Qatar Airways, FlyDubai, and SalamAir.
The Bangladesh embassy in Saudi Arabia has urged expatriates to remain alert as the situation develops.
Minister Shama Obaid has stated that Riyadh-bound passengers may be flown via Dammam or Medina to mitigate the impact of the layanan restrictions.
caption:
Over 5,000 passengers are stranded at Dhaka airport after 51 flights to Saudi Arabia were disrupted.

Saudi Arabian airport restrictions have caused the disruption of 51 flights from Dhaka to various destinations in the Kingdom, leaving 5,418 passengers stranded.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the disruptions occurred between Saturday night and Monday afternoon.

Of the 51 affected flights, 12 were direct flights, including those operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Saudi Arabian Airlines, and Riyadh Air.

The remaining 39 flights were transit flights operated by carriers such as IndiGo, Emirates, Qatar Airways, FlyDubai, and SalamAir.

The Bangladesh embassy in Saudi Arabia has urged expatriates to remain alert as the situation develops.

Minister Shama Obaid has stated that Riyadh-bound passengers may be flown via Dammam or Medina to mitigate the impact of the layanan restrictions.

headline: 5 units responding as fire breaks out at Chawkbazar market
summary: The blaze erupted at Manzur Khan Plaza in Old Dhaka, starting from a shop on the sixth floor.
details: A fire broke out at Manzur Khan Plaza, a market in Old Dhaka’s Chawkbazar area on Monday afternoon.
Fire Service and Civil Defence Media Officer Talha Bin Jasim stated that the alert was received at 5:04 PM, with operations beginning approximately 20 minutes later.
The blaze reportedly started at a shop located on the sixth floor of the market building.
Five units from the Fire Service and Civil Defence are currently working to bring the fire under control.
The cause of the fire and the total extent of the damage have not yet been immediately known.
caption:
A fire has erupted at Manzur Khan Plaza in Old Dhaka's Chawkbazar. Five fire service units are on the scene.

A fire broke out at Manzur Khan Plaza, a market in Old Dhaka’s Chawkbazar area on Monday afternoon.

Fire Service and Civil Defence Media Officer Talha Bin Jasim stated that the alert was received at 5:04 PM, with operations beginning approximately 20 minutes later.

The blaze reportedly started at a shop located on the sixth floor of the market building.

Five units from the Fire Service and Civil Defence are currently working to bring the fire under control.

The cause of the fire and the total extent of the damage have not yet been immediately known.
